paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: you can't see how it all turns out, so get to work anyway. The Teacher says to "Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again." (Ecclesiastes 11:1) He also says to share what you have, "for you do not know what disaster may befall the land." (Ecclesiastes 11:2) Open hands are the wise kind of hands.

Now, the Teacher knows how we are. Some of us would watch the wind and the clouds until the sun goes down, waiting for a perfect sign. But "He who watches the wind will fail to sow, and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap." (Ecclesiastes 11:4) You cannot understand "the work of God, the Maker of all things" (Ecclesiastes 11:5), so the answer isn't to figure Him out first. It's to "Sow your seed in the morning, and do not rest your hands in the evening." (Ecclesiastes 11:6) God is the Maker, and you get to be the one who plants.

And you can do it with joy. "Light is sweet, and it pleases the eyes to see the sun." (Ecclesiastes 11:7) The Teacher says to "rejoice" in all your years, and to remember that the days of darkness will be many. (Ecclesiastes 11:8) I know a little about dark days, friend, and I can tell you the light is still sweet. So plant, share and rejoice today, and leave the tomorrow part to the Maker of all things.
